claims.text: Rapid quenching creates a highly homogeneous atomic distribution in noble metal high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles.
Rapid quenching minimizes elemental or phase segregation relative to slower cooling.
Rapid quenching induces compressive lattice strain in the nanoparticles.
Rapidly quenched nanoparticles provide more reliable catalytic performance than slowly cooled nanoparticles.
Rapid quenching preserves high mixing entropy.
Preserved high mixing entropy ensures a random and homogeneous distribution of noble-metal atoms.
Reduced phase segregation promotes compressive lattice strain.
Compressive lattice strain stabilizes catalytic active sites.
Stabilization of catalytic active sites enhances catalytic performance.
Rapidly quenched nanoparticles will have statistically higher catalytic conversion rates than the slow-cooled baseline.
Rapidly quenched nanoparticles will have more uniform phase composition and lattice parameters than the slow-cooled baseline.
Slow-cooled materials may exhibit elemental segregation and less favorable lattice-strain characteristics.
The proposed mechanism should hold under moderate-temperature oxidizing catalytic conditions and for compositions capable of attaining high mixing entropy.
The magnitude of catalytic enhancement likely depends on the specific noble-metal composition.
